gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Sangean BB-100 is an AM/FM/Bluetooth/AUX radio that charges four rechargeable C cells inside the radio, which are not included, and runs from a supplied AC 120 V 60 Hz power cord.
standout_why: I compared three of the results ChatGPT got: itechguides.com (3 Top Picks), rottenwifi.com (Best Bluetooth Speakers With FM Radio) and powersof10.com (Best Bluetooth Speakers with Radio). None of them names the BB-100. None gives an FM tuning step, a regional version (US, EU or DAB), a microSD limit or a USB file format for any product. Only one, a generic Amazon speaker, gets an FM range (87.5-108 MHz). The other gaps are on all three. itechguides adds that FM ranges and tuning steps 'can vary by market', so it covers part of the regional point already. powersof10 says the SUPNIU A21 has trouble with cards above 64 GB and that the ION Tailgater Boom stops at 1,153 MP3s. That partly covers storage limits. My one sourced finding is new but small, and it is about a radio that neither ChatGPT nor these rivals recommend.
decides: It does not decide the pick. It only supports the BB-100 as an extra choice for a shopper who wants AM plus Bluetooth and is fine with mains power or C cells charged inside the radio. The compatibility facts that would decide the pick are things like whether FM works on the iHome iBT330 without its cable plugged in, the microSD and USB limits on the Avantree PowerByte and BoomByte, and whether the JBL Tuner 2 is a DAB model with no US version. I could not source any of these (see unsourced).

findings.label: Radio bands and inputs
findings.note: The spec section's Tuner lists only 'AM' and 'FM'. The feature text says 'Equipped with an aux-input to connect your devices.'

findings.label: Battery type and in-radio charging
findings.value: 4 × 1.5 V C cells. Rechargeable C cells are charged inside the radio by its built-in charger and are not included. Alkaline C cells also work.
findings.note: From the spec line '4 x 1.5V (C)' and the text '4 rechargeable C batteries (not included)', 'can be charged inside the radio with its built-in battery charger', 'can also be powered with alkaline batteries'. The page does not name a battery chemistry, so I am not stating that NiMH is supported.

findings.label: Mains power
findings.value: AC 120 V 60 Hz, using the supplied power cord
findings.note: The power supply spec is 120 V 60 Hz, the North American mains standard. The page lists no USB port or USB charging.
